description:

WHY THE SPLIT EXISTS. governor's 16:33Z re-plan ruling on R3-5 says a module-cached constant cannot carry a store-scoped value, and that under Rail 8(A) the plan must now own every caller its change reaches. Measured consequence: R3-5's own roster then needs TWELVE distinct affectedFiles (matcher .ts + .js bridge + its new suite, contracts, service, edges.test, refusals.test, service.test, test-fixtures, and the three foreign callers). The daemon HARD-REJECTS a plan above 10 distinct files. Per the global rail, "if naming every consumer would breach the row's path cap, that is a SPLIT signal at plan time" — so the caller migration is carved here and R3-5 keeps the matcher.

THE DEFECT THIS ROW FIXES, measured by worker-a224437e at HEAD e3d20791 (comment-215633dc5ab24672aff04fc32b7b1704 on R3-5). `supersedeInput()` at apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-test-fixtures.ts:185 is ZERO-ARG and returns `{ approval: decidedApproval() }` — one immutable record shared by six caller files. Its value is not a constant of the system; it is STORE-SCOPED. Three consumers each need a DIFFERENT one:
- apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-context-prelaunch.test.ts:703-712 seals and requests successorContent(NODE_KEY) where NODE_KEY is node-a, while the shared record is node-b. One immutable exactRevisionHash cannot equal both content-addressed successor bodies. Refuses GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_APPROVAL_REVISION_MISMATCH at :713.
- apps/daemon/src/planning/active-graph-slot-ordering.test.ts:78 and apps/daemon/src/planning/active-graph-slot.test.ts:215 drive the two-goal / file-backed worlds, whose predecessor boundHashes differ from the canonical world. Named failures: ordering:84 expected false to be true; slot:225 same; slot:258 expected CONCURRENT_ACTIVATION/DURABLE_STORE but received APPROVAL_BUDGET_MISMATCH/GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_SERVICE.

THIS ROW SHIPS NO RED, BEFORE OR AFTER. The R3-5 matcher does NOT exist at HEAD (apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts is untracked WIP on R3-5's row and is NOT yours — do not commit it, do not import it). So nothing refuses these records today: deriving them from each caller's own store is a strictly more accurate no-op now, and is exactly what makes R3-5's guard satisfiable later. If your change reds any of the six suites, you have changed behaviour and must stop.

SCOPE, exactly four files. Add a store-scoped successor-bound approval builder to graph-supersede-test-fixtures.ts and migrate ONLY the three foreign callers to it. KEEP `supersedeInput()`'s zero-arg call shape working for the in-roster callers (graph-supersede-refusals.test.ts x19 and graph-supersede-service.test.ts x12) — those two files belong to R3-5 and are DIRTY with its uncommitted steps 2-4 WIP right now; touching them here is a hunk-granular collision with live foreign work and is forbidden. implementationPlan.description:
STEP 2 — THE STORE-SCOPED BUILDER in apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-test-fixtures.ts. Discharges DoD item 2.

Add `successorBoundApproval(store, nodeKey = SUCCESSOR_NODE_KEY)` returning an `ApprovalDecisionRecord` whose seven binding fields are DERIVED BY READING THE STORE, never written as literals. Construct the record through the SAME core path `decidedApproval()` uses — `approvalRecord(...)` then `applyApprovalCommand(...)`, throwing on a refused verdict — so it is a genuinely DECIDED record, not a hand-assembled object.

The seven derivations, each from the production reader that already yields it (these are exactly what R3-5's matcher compares against; deriving them any other way re-freezes the defect one level down):
1. exactRevisionHash — `successorContent(nodeKey).graphContentHash` (the existing fixture helper at :42; SUCCESSOR_GRAPH_CONTENT_HASH at :71 is built this same way). This is what makes node-a and node-b differ and is the whole point of the row.
2. approvedNodeScope — the successor's node key set, derived from the same `nodeIds: [nodeKey]` that `successorContent` feeds `journeyAuthority`. Not a hardcoded `["node-b"]`.
3. budgetRef — the PREDECESSOR's `boundHashes.budgetHash`, read via `replayGraphRevisionEvents` over the history of `graphRevisionAggregateId(PROJECT_ID, <active revisionId>)`. This is the field the two-goal and file-backed worlds diverge on.
4. criteriaRef — `readApprovedCriteria(store, PROJECT_ID, GOAL_ID).criteriaDigest`.
5. planQualityAssessmentRef — predecessor `boundHashes.qualityHash`.
6. applicablePolicyRef — predecessor `boundHashes.policyHash`.
7. policyDecisionRef — `null` (task-9fb4e53d will later replace absence with a durable digest; leave it null).

Throw a clear fixture error if any read refuses or `boundHashes` is null — a fixture that silently yields an undefined field would produce a mismatch that reads as a production bug.

ALSO give `supersedeInput` an OPTIONAL override so the zero-arg call shape is preserved: `supersedeInput(overrides: Partial<GraphSupersedeInput> = {})`, defaulting `approval` to `decidedApproval()` exactly as today. A REQUIRED parameter is forbidden — nineteen call sites in refusals.test.ts and twelve in service.test.ts are out of scope and must keep compiling untouched.

DO NOT import R3-5's untracked `graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts`. Use the underlying production readers directly.
implementationPlan.note: Added successorBoundApproval(store, nodeKey = SUCCESSOR_NODE_KEY) plus two private helpers (revisionHistory, predecessorBinding, decodedSuccessor). All seven fields derived by reading the caller's store: exactRevisionHash from successorContent(nodeKey).graphContentHash; approvedNodeScope from decodeGraphContent(...).content.nodeAuthority.authorities.map(nodeKey) rather than a literal; budgetRef/qualityHash/policyHash from replayGraphRevisionEvents over graphRevisionAggregateId(PROJECT_ID, readCurrentActiveGraph(store).revisionId); criteriaRef from readApprovedCriteria(store, PROJECT_ID, GOAL_ID).criteriaDigest; policyDecisionRef null. Built through approvalRecord + applyApprovalCommand, the same core path decidedApproval() uses, throwing on a refused verdict, an unreadable criteria read, an absent active predecessor, or null boundHashes. supersedeInput now takes Partial<GraphSupersedeInput> = {} defaulting approval to decidedApproval(), so all 31 out-of-scope zero-arg call sites are untouched. Did NOT import R3-5's untracked matcher. File is 276 lines. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` now reports ONLY the two disclosed foreign errors (daemon-command-edges.ts:60, daemon-store-dependencies.ts:178, TS2353 subscriberId); zero errors in any owned path.
